label: Using your time
rationale: The jikan o verbs for what you do with time: put it into something, set it aside, make it, kill it.
mixUps: English spend, take, make and kill map to kakeru, toru, tsukuru and tsubusu (crush), never korosu; how long something takes stays jikan ga kakaru, and spending time with people is sugosu.

targets.english: put time into, take time over
targets.verbSense: hang; put on; spend (time or money on something)
targets.trap: 'I spent three hours on it' is sanjikan kaketa (or kakatta), not sugoshita: sugosu is for spending time somewhere or with someone.
partners: tema (effort: tema o kakeru = go to the trouble)
targets.use: For spending time on something on purpose, mostly as kakete before another verb: jikan kakete tsukutta (I put real time into making it). With an amount, jikan drops: sanjikan kaketa. 'Take your time' is usually yukkuri de ii yo; jikan kakete ii yo is for a task: jikkuri jikan kakete ii yo.
targets.notes: Its intransitive partner jikan ga kakaru is how long something takes; kakeru is you choosing to spend it.

example.romaji: kore, kekkou jikan kakete tsukutta n da.
example.ja: これ、けっこう時間かけて作ったんだ。
example.english: I put quite a lot of time into making this.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa kekkou jikan o kakete tsukutta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: これはけっこう時間をかけて作ったんです。
examplePolite.english: I put quite a lot of time into making this.

targets.english: set aside time, take up time
targets.verbSense: take; get (here: take or set aside time)
targets.trap: English 'it takes an hour' leads to toru, but how long something takes is kakaru: ichijikan kakaru. toru is someone setting time aside, or taking up yours: jikan totte kurete arigatou, ojikan torasete sumimasen.
targets.use: Mostly in thanks and apologies: jikan totte kurete arigatou (thanks for making time), ojikan torasete sumimasen (sorry to take up your time). It also means setting time aside: kondo chanto jikan toru ne.
targets.notes: jikan toreru? asks if someone can spare time. A short polite thank-you, (kichou na) ojikan o arigatou gozaimashita, is also fine, and formal thanks use saku: ojikan o saite itadaite.

example.romaji: kyou wa jikan totte kurete arigatou.
example.ja: 今日は時間取ってくれてありがとう。

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa ojikan totte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はお時間取っていただいて、ありがとうございました。
examplePolite.english: Thank you for making time today.

targets.use: Said when promising to fit someone in, often in the potential: raishuu nara jikan tsukureru yo. In thanks it's jikan tsukutte kurete arigatou.
targets.notes: Close to jikan o toru: tsukuru stresses squeezing time out of a busy schedule. Both work in thanks (jikan tsukutte kurete arigatou / jikan totte kurete arigatou).

example.ja: 来週なら時間作れるよ。
example.english: I can make time next week.

examplePolite.romaji: raishuu nara jikan o tsukuremasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 来週なら時間を作れますよ。
examplePolite.english: I can make time next week.

targets.trap: Not jikan o korosu: killing time is tsubusu, 'crush'.
targets.use: Said when you're early or waiting for someone: kafe de jikan tsubushiteru ne. The noun himatsubushi (something to pass the time) is just as common: himatsubushi ni sumaho miteta.
targets.notes: tsubusu also means flatten (akikan o tsubusu). A day off that gets eaten up is yasumi ga tsubureta.

example.romaji: hayaku tsuita kara, kafe de jikan tsubushiteru.
example.ja: 早く着いたから、カフェで時間潰してる。
example.english: I got here early, so I'm killing time in a café.

examplePolite.romaji: hayaku tsuita node, kafe de jikan o tsubushitemasu.
examplePolite.ja: 早く着いたので、カフェで時間を潰してます。
examplePolite.english: I got here early, so I'm killing time in a café.
